problem: Large language models struggle to scale instruction tuning across heterogeneous task mixtures due to gradient interference and bandwidth-heavy synchronization during centralized training.
approach: MERIT decentralizes training by partitioning diverse instruction tasks along gradient conflict axes, training each partition independently without communication, then merging models via token-weighted averaging that acts as spectral filtering.
contribution: On Qwen2.5-VL-3B with 136 Vision-FLAN tasks, MERIT improves 8-benchmark average from 54.3 to 57.0 without inter-partition communication overhead.

problem: Hybrid sequence models combining Transformers and state-space models lack principled understanding of when and why they outperform their constituent models.
approach: The paper constructs hybrid models that provably solve selective copying and associative recall tasks with small size and working memory, while showing non-hybrid models require either many parameters or large working memory.
contribution: Learned hybrids outperform non-hybrids with up to 6× fewer parameters, showing stronger length generalization and out-of-distribution robustness.

problem: The Gaussian mechanism for differential privacy is widely used but lacks theoretical justification that it achieves optimal privacy-utility tradeoffs.
approach: The work provides asymptotic analysis of additive-noise mechanisms and develops Spherical Generalized Gamma mechanisms that extend and improve upon the Gaussian and ℓ2 mechanisms in low-dimensional settings.
contribution: Proves that as dimension T→∞, no additive-noise mechanism asymptotically improves the Gaussian mechanism; identifies new members of the Gamma family outperforming both Gaussian and ℓ2 mechanisms in low dimensions.

problem: Multi-domain graph pre-training requires jointly training all source graphs at high computational cost, despite potential data redundancy across domains.
approach: MDGMIX uses boundary-aware subgraph mixing to select challenging cross-domain subgraphs and applies hierarchical discrimination to decouple shared patterns from domain-specific patterns.
contribution: MDGMIX consistently outperforms baselines in few-shot classification while achieving superior time and memory efficiency on multi-domain graph transfer.

problem: Test-time optimization of generative models for reward maximization leads to reward hacking and is computationally expensive for practical use.
approach: Gradient preconditioning projects reward gradients onto a white Gaussian noise feasible set with blockwise norm constraints, achieving O(N log N) complexity via FFT-matching projection.
contribution: On FLUX with four reward models, the method reaches comparable Aesthetic Score using only 30% of the wall-clock time required by regularization-based baselines.

problem: The Lipschitz constant of neural networks is not well understood at random initialization and during training; prior bounds grow logarithmically with width.
approach: For networks with smooth activations, the work establishes width-independent upper bounds on the local Lipschitz constant at random initialization and throughout lazy training.
contribution: Proves that the local Lipschitz constant does not increase with network width, closing a gap in the theory of generalization for overparameterized networks.

problem: Multimodal LLMs suffer from vision-language misalignment where textual responses do not factually align with given text-image inputs due to causal attention limiting cross-modal information flow.
approach: Modality-Mutual Attention (MMA) unlocks causal attention to enable image tokens to attend to text tokens, allowing earlier modalities to incorporate information from later modalities.
contribution: MMA achieves +6.2% average improvement across 3 LLM backbones on 12 multimodal understanding benchmarks without adding parameters.

problem: Transformer-based tabular foundation models have quadratic complexity in dataset size, limiting scalability to large-scale tabular datasets.
approach: TACO compresses the training dataset in latent space, enabling in-context learning without the quadratic overhead of attention mechanisms.
contribution: On TabArena, TACO is up to 94× faster in inference and uses up to 97% less memory compared to state-of-the-art tabular Transformers while maintaining performance.

problem: Diffusion-based reinforcement learning has substantial training and inference overhead due to the iterative generative process.
approach: Mean Flow Policy Optimization (MFPO) uses few-step flow models instead of diffusion models to represent policies, optimized under maximum entropy RL via soft policy iteration.
contribution: MFPO achieves performance comparable to diffusion-based baselines while considerably reducing training and inference time on MuJoCo and DeepMind Control Suite.

problem: Documentation for code is traditionally written for human readability but should instead serve as precise playbooks for coding agents; refining one entity's documentation can invalidate dependent callers.
approach: DocSearch formulates agent-oriented documentation as a black-box optimization problem using a dependency-guided bi-level search: priority search over entity DAG with callee-before-caller order, and beam search over refinements using error message sampling.
contribution: DocSearch achieves 90.7% solve rate on DevEval+ with GPT-4o, outperforming the strongest baseline by 32.6%, with effective transfer across programming languages.

problem: Hypergraph contrastive learning emphasizes instance discrimination via uniformity, which causes semantic flattening where the hierarchical structure of hyperedges collapses into a flat representation.
approach: HyperDepth recovers semantic depth via a decoupled spectral encoding scheme with adaptive gating and an energy-based hierarchical alignment module that attaches a learnable prototype tree.
contribution: HyperDepth achieves equilibrium embeddings that preserve semantic depth while retaining instance-level discrimination on 15 hypergraph datasets across supervised and self-supervised settings.

problem: Standard contrastive learning on hypergraphs ignores multi-level semantics, pushing embeddings apart indiscriminately and causing hierarchical structure to collapse.
approach: HyperDepth coordinates spectral and geometric signals through decoupled encoding with adaptive gating for instance discrimination and energy-based prototype-tree alignment for hierarchical structure.
contribution: On 15 hypergraph datasets, HyperDepth provably preserves semantic depth under a frequency-separation assumption while maintaining instance-level discrimination.

problem: Auditory attention decoding from EEG overlooks crucial phase information, limiting the ability to distinguish neural patterns from noise in the frequency domain.
approach: PCRNet uses a Temporal Context Calibration module for multi-scale temporal attention and a Dual-Domain Integration module with phase-guided spectral filtering to refine real and imaginary components separately.
contribution: PCRNet outperforms state-of-the-art on three public auditory attention datasets, particularly under challenging ultra-short 0.1-second windows.

problem: Diffusion language models lack effective post-training and reinforcement learning techniques, especially for downstream reasoning tasks.
approach: AGRPO optimizes individual denoising steps rather than full sequences via Markovian policy gradients, enabling unbiased gradient updates with a novel timestep estimation scheme.
contribution: AGRPO achieves +59.4% on Countdown and +69.7% on Sudoku over the base LLaDA model, exceeding comparable diffusion-RL methods.

problem: Existing idea evaluation methods suffer from narrow knowledge horizons, flattened evaluation dimensions, and bias in LLM-as-a-Judge approaches.
approach: InnoEval uses heterogeneous deep knowledge search to ground evidence from diverse sources and employs an innovation review board with distinct academic backgrounds for multi-dimensional evaluation.
contribution: InnoEval outperforms baselines in point-wise, pair-wise, and group-wise evaluation tasks with judgment patterns and consensus aligned with human experts.

problem: Understanding how cellular morphology, gene expression, and spatial context jointly shape tissue function at high resolution is difficult; existing methods analyze modalities in isolation.
approach: SPATIA fuses morphology, gene expression, and spatial context through multi-level generative and predictive models, using confidence-aware optimal transport reweighting and morphology-profile alignment.
contribution: SPATIA improves generative fidelity by 8% and predictive accuracy by up to 3% on 12 tasks across 25.9 million cell-gene pairs from 17 tissues.

problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods like LoRA operate in isolation within each modality, limiting their ability to capture cross-modal interactions for multimodal tasks.
approach: CoLA extends LoRA with a dedicated inter-modal adaptation pathway alongside intra-modal paths, enabling dual-path design for effective cross-modal learning without interference.
contribution: CoLA achieves ~3% relative gain on vision-language benchmarks and ~2% on audio-visual benchmarks while maintaining parameter efficiency, enabling the first multi-task PEFT framework for visual grounding.

problem: Real-world control systems must balance multiple competing continuous objectives while minimizing instability, but existing frameworks focus on binary states.
approach: Lazy Graph-LinUCB performs lazy updates on continuous states under a dependency graph, minimizing switching costs while maintaining near-optimal regret through asynchronous updates and adaptive graph learning.
contribution: Structural exploitation reduces movement costs by more than a factor of three in heterogeneous systems while maintaining similar cumulative losses.

problem: Large language models face continuous domain shifts during testing; existing continual test-time adaptation methods struggle to balance adaptability and stability due to dense model architectures.
approach: TiME uses mixture-of-experts routing via asymmetric co-optimal transport with semantic space alignment to ensure reliable routing across unseen shifting domains.
contribution: TiME outperforms baselines in continual test-time adaptation for LLMs on shifting domains.

problem: Large language models answer questions involving negation incorrectly, despite having internal components that process negation correctly.
approach: The work identifies two mechanisms: attention heads that suppress negated concepts, and constructive mechanisms that represent negative phrases as vectors; combining observational and causal interpretability techniques shows the constructive mechanism is more prominent.
contribution: Ablating late-layer attention improves negation accuracy; models implement both suppression and construction mechanisms for negation, with construction being dominant.

problem: Large language models struggle with the strict procedural logic and accuracy required by biological protocols, limiting autonomous scientific experimentation.
approach: BioProBench provides a corpus of 27,000 human-written protocols and 550,000+ task instances; ProAgent is developed grounded in this corpus to advance procedural reasoning in biology.
contribution: While general comprehension is high, LLM performance drops on tasks requiring deep reasoning, quantitative precision, and safety awareness; ProAgent substantially advances state-of-the-art.

problem: Neural network wavefunctions lack principled benchmarking and systematic understanding of expressivity and scaling properties across quantum domains.
approach: WF-Bench provides a comprehensive dataset spanning topological states, Wigner crystals, and superconducting wavefunctions, with a systematic benchmarking protocol using wavefunction fidelity as the uniform metric.
contribution: Empirical scaling laws characterize representability dependence on system size and model parameters; WF-Bench establishes a unified framework for evaluating and comparing neural network wavefunctions.

problem: Language models respond inconsistently to translation-equivalent prompts across languages, undermining multilingual system reliability.
approach: PCO (penalized consistency optimization) couples response divergence with KL penalty to a reference language; DCO (direct consistency optimization) provides a tractable surrogate optimizable off-policy.
contribution: DCO significantly improves crosslingual consistency across 26 languages and diverse models, outperforming existing methods and enabling targeted alignment of low-resource languages.

problem: Existing self-rewarding language models suffer from synchronized improvement of chosen and rejected responses, narrowing their representational difference and weakening preference learning signals.
approach: Temporal Self-Rewarding strategically coordinates past, present, and future generations: Anchored Rejection fixes rejected responses using the past model while Future-Guided Chosen curates chosen samples using next-generation predictions.
contribution: On Llama3.1-8B, reaches 29.44 win rate on AlpacaEval 2.0, outperforming self-rewarding baseline (19.69) by 9.75 percentage points with superior out-of-distribution generalization.

problem: Notification dispatch must optimize complex trade-offs across timing, presentation style, multiple outcomes, and platform constraints with small-effect uplift estimation.
approach: BUOPLR decouples uplift estimation from constrained optimization: learns bundle-level multi-outcome uplift via an architecture capturing cross-treatment relationships, then performs scalable assignment via Lagrangian relaxation.
contribution: BUOPLR outperforms state-of-the-art in offline experiments and increases DAU by 0.5% in online A/B tests on Kuaishou, deployed at 100+ million daily users.

problem: Large multimodal models have high inference-time overhead; existing methods prune visual tokens at prefill assuming static visual evidence, but evidence is step-dependent during reasoning.
approach: VisionPulse computes lightweight visual attention mass to estimate step-wise retention budget and retains only critical tokens per decoding step, filtering redundant visual context.
contribution: VisionPulse retains 5% of visual tokens per step with 11.2% shortened reasoning traces while keeping accuracy nearly unchanged.

problem: Scene graph generation is limited by scarce annotations and long-tailed relational distributions; training-free methods rely on flat structures and produce hallucinated relations.
approach: HSGG uses bidirectional hierarchical entity perception for multi-level scene hierarchies, then infers valid relations via geometry-aware filtering and geometry-grounded contrastive relation decoding.
contribution: HSGG generalizes to unseen objects and predicates without training, substantially reduces relational hallucinations, and improves downstream reasoning performance.

problem: Theoretical results on neural network expressivity are derived under exact arithmetic and do not apply to floating-point implementations with finite precision and rounding errors.
approach: The work studies floating-point ReLU networks with floating-point parameters and operations, determining minimum depth and width for representing all functions from floating-point vectors to floating-point numbers.
contribution: Proves minimum depth is exactly three; minimum width for representing all functions from F^d to F is between 2d and 2d+4, with tighter bounds for non-negative floats.

problem: Static conditional value-at-risk objectives in safety-critical MDPs lack recursive Bellman decomposition; classical state augmentation leads to sparse rewards and degenerate fixed points.
approach: A novel state-augmentation formulation yields a Bellman operator with dense per-step rewards and contracting properties; value iteration and Q-learning algorithms use discretized augmented states.
contribution: Algorithms successfully learn CVaR-sensitive policies with convergence guarantees and approximation error bounds, achieving effective performance-safety trade-offs.

problem: Federated learning with heterogeneous hardware and non-IID data requires sub-model extraction, but existing methods rely on coarse-grained stochastic selection or rigid rule-based neuron selection.
approach: SpineFL decomposes layers into a mandatory backbone shared by all sub-models and a dynamic portion; activation-guided pruning selects neurons probabilistically based on historical activation frequency.
contribution: SpineFL addresses parameter conflicts under non-IID data while enabling comprehensive parameter optimization through diverse neuron selection.

problem: TabPFN, a foundation model for tabular in-context learning, is vulnerable to label shift and overfits to the majority class in training data.
approach: DistPFN performs test-time posterior adjustment by rescaling predicted class probabilities to downweight training prior influence; DistPFN-T adds temperature scaling for adaptive adjustment strength.
contribution: On 250+ OpenML datasets, DistPFN substantially improves classification under label shift while maintaining performance without label shift, without architectural modification.

problem: Coverless image steganography lacks robust access control to selectively reveal different hidden contents to different authorized users.
approach: MIDAS uses a training-free diffusion-based framework with Random Basis mechanism for suppressing residual structural information and Latent Vector Fusion for user-specific access control.
contribution: MIDAS outperforms training-free baselines in access control functionality, stego quality, diversity, robustness to noise, and resistance to steganalysis.

problem: Reasoning chains with pretrained generative models can be expensive and often pursue unpromising directions, wasting computation.
approach: Re-FORC trains a lightweight adapter to predict expected future rewards as a function of future thinking tokens, enabling early stopping and optimized model-length selection.
contribution: Re-FORC reduces compute by up to 24% via early stopping, reaches 1.7 pp higher accuracy while needing 12% less compute, and increases accuracy by 8.8 pp via adaptive test-time scaling.

problem: LLMs with chain-of-thought reasoning suffer from excessive token consumption inflating inference costs despite achieving strong performance.
approach: Batched Contextual Reinforcement trains models to solve N problems simultaneously within a shared context window, creating an implicit token budget that yields controllable throughput.
contribution: BCR reduces token usage by 15.8%-62.6% while maintaining or improving accuracy; identifies a task-scaling law where per-problem token usage decreases monotonically with concurrent problems.

problem: Robotic manipulation policy learning design choices like action space representation are guided by ad-hoc heuristics, lacking systematic understanding of how these choices affect policy learnability and stability.
approach: Large-scale empirical study examining 13,000+ real-world rollouts and 500+ trained models across temporal and spatial action dimensions, dissecting trade-offs systematically.
contribution: Delta actions consistently improve performance over absolute representations; joint-space and task-space representations offer complementary strengths favoring stability and generalization respectively.

problem: Existing supervised alignment of pretrained vision and language models requires millions of paired samples; semi-supervised alignment with unpaired data is unexplored.
approach: SOTAlign uses a two-stage framework: recovers coarse shared geometry from limited paired data via linear teacher, then refines on unpaired samples via optimal-transport-based divergence preserving relational structure.
contribution: SOTAlign effectively leverages unpaired images and text, learns robust joint embeddings across datasets and encoder pairs, significantly outperforming supervised and semi-supervised baselines.

problem: Fine-tuning language models on narrowly scoped objectives leads to emergent out-of-domain misaligned behaviors even though target behavior is learned.
approach: BLOCK-EM identifies a small set of internal features reliably controlling misaligned behavior and constrains these features during fine-tuning to discourage their strengthening.
contribution: Blocking features achieves up to 95% relative reduction in emergent misalignment with no degradation in model quality or target-task performance on six fine-tuning domains.

problem: Inferring temporal processes from static single-cell RNA snapshots is difficult; current approaches are sensitive to overfitting and lack consideration of biological variability.
approach: Combines latent heteroscedastic Gaussian process approximated via Hilbert space methods with optimal transport to align generated and observed population distributions, incorporating cell-specific latent time and type conditioning.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on complex interpolation and extrapolation benchmarks; introduces gradient-based strategy for inferring perturbation trajectories.

problem: Visual reinforcement learning with bisimulation objectives is limited by fixed, pre-specified global norms for measuring latent state similarity, which may be overly restrictive or degenerate.
approach: PAMD parameterizes a positive-definite, pair-conditioned Mahalanobis distance as a plug-in for bisimulation-based methods, offering more expressive yet structured alternatives to fixed metrics.
contribution: PAMD substantially improves final performance of several recent bisimulation-based RL algorithms on visual MuJoCo continuous-control tasks.

problem: Omni-modal LLMs enabling real-time interaction across video, audio, and text suffer from prohibitive computational costs due to quadratic complexity of processing streaming inputs.
approach: OmniFit uses Layer-Adaptive Heterogeneity Profiling to dynamically allocate budgets based on layer-wise redundancy, and Alignment-Rectified Token Selection to identify semantically aligned tokens.
contribution: OmniFit retains 98% of model performance with 20% token usage, achieving up to 2.31× end-to-end inference speedup and 2.5× VRAM saving compared to state-of-the-art.
